$comment: Generated by `node scripts/build-ui-catalogue.mjs` from src/ui; edit the code, not this file. Import everything from `@/ui`. hasElementProps: other props pass to the rendered element. figma.node is a node id in the Figma file below. A story opens at http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/<id> (npm run storybook).

Button.description:
A text button. Extra props (aria-*, a Tooltip's handlers) pass straight to
the `<button>`, which is `type="button"` unless told otherwise.

isDisabled.description: Drops input and dims the button. It stays focusable, so a tooltip can say why.

isLoading.description: Drops input and swaps the leading glyph (or, with none, adds one) for a spinner.

loadingLabel.description: The label while loading ("Retrying…"), when it should say so.

IconButton.description:
A square, icon-only button with a tooltip. Disabled and loading work as on
Button. Extra props pass straight to the `<button>`.

iconSize.description: 16, or 14 for a glyph that reads large (Play). The spinner matches it.

isDisabled.description: Drops input and dims the button. It stays focusable, so its tooltip can say why.

isLoading.description: Drops input and swaps the glyph for a spinner.

label.description: Names the button (it has no visible text) and is its tooltip, unless `tooltip` says more.

tooltip.description: The tooltip, when it should say more than the label (a help button's hint).

Link.description:
A link at the size of the text it sits in. With `onClick` it opens another
view in the app (All results, View timeline) and ends in a caret; with
`href` it opens a real address in a new window, ends in an arrow, and says
so to a screen reader.

href.description: A real address, opened in a new window.

isDisabled.description: Drops input and dims the link. It stays focusable, so a tooltip can say why.

StretchedLink.description:
A transparent link stretched over its positioned container (a card, a row),
so a click anywhere opens the view the container summarises. It's a link
to a screen reader: it moves to another view rather than acting. A control
in the container raises itself above it and stays a sibling, never nested.
Its focus ring follows the container's corners, just inside the edge.
`data-stretched-link` lets the container style itself while it has focus;
`className` can round the ring where the container's own corners don't (a
list's first and last rows).

label.description: Names it: it has no text of its own, since the container's content shows through.

Menu.description:
An overflow menu: a kebab that opens a short list of actions. The arrow keys
move between items, Escape or a click outside closes it, and focus returns
to the kebab.

isOpen.description: Controlled open state; leave both out to let the menu keep its own.

MenuContent.description: The dropdown, under the kebab and lined up with its right edge.

onClick.description: Runs the action; the menu closes.

MenuTrigger.description: The kebab that opens the menu. `className` is for where it sits (a row that reveals it on hover).

label.description: Names the kebab, which has no visible text: "Options for Google".

action.description: A button inside the field's border, after the text: a TextFieldAction.

className.description: On the field as a whole: its place in the form.

feedback.description:
Under the field and read as its description: a hint, a result, an error.
A live region, so it's announced as it changes.

isInvalid.description: The value failed to parse or check: a red border, and `aria-invalid`.

TextFieldAction.description: The button inside a TextField's border (Test). Disabled and loading work as on Button.

loadingLabel.description: Names the button while loading, when only a spinner shows ("Testing").

Toggle.description: An on/off switch for a setting.

aria-describedby.description: Id of the text that explains the setting, read after the label.

label.description: Names the switch, which shows no text of its own.

SegmentedControl.description:
A few mutually exclusive options side by side: a radio group with one Tab
stop, the arrow keys choosing the next or previous option.

aria-describedby.description: Id of the text that explains it.

aria-label.description: Names the group, or the id of the text that does.

Dialog.description:
A modal dialog: title, optional description and close button, a recessed
body, an optional footnote, and a footer of actions. Focus moves in and
stays inside while it's open, the page behind is inert, and focus returns to
the opener on close.
Escape, the close button, Cancel and a click on the backdrop all call
`onClose`.

Render it inside a DialogRoot, which opens it and plays its leave animation.

actions.description: The footer's buttons, main action last.

cancelLabel.description: Label for a button before the actions that closes the dialog.

canClose.description: False while something runs that closing would abandon: every way out is off.

children.description: The body, in a recessed well. Omit for a dialog that's only a header and actions.

description.description: The line under the title, read as the dialog's description.

footnote.description: A line under the body, on the panel: a caption or status.

isDirty.description: Holds input the user typed: a stray click on the backdrop won't throw it away.

DialogRoot.description:
Opens and closes a Dialog. Its children mount when `isOpen` turns true and
stay mounted until the Dialog's leave animation ends after it turns false,
so the component that renders the Dialog (and its state) lives only that long.

children.description: The component that renders the Dialog: mounted while open and while it leaves.

Tooltip.description:
A short hint on hover and keyboard focus, portalled so a card's clipping
never cuts it. A click hides it. Screen readers get the content as the
trigger's description, unless it repeats the trigger's name.

align.description:
For `top` and `bottom`, the trigger edge the bubble lines up with: `end`
(the default) grows it leftward from the trigger's right edge, so a trigger
near the window's right edge never spills it; `start` grows it rightward.

children.type: ReactElement<{ 'aria-label'?: string | undefined; 'aria-describedby'?: string | undefined; }, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>>
children.description: The trigger: one element that takes a ref and props (a button, an icon's span).

content.description: Shown on hover and keyboard focus.

isDisabled.description: Never opens: for content that would be stale (a rating while a new test runs).

maxWidth.description: The bubble's width (px) before its content wraps; wider for one-line content like a hostname.

shouldDescribe.description:
False when the content only repeats the trigger's accessible name, so a
screen reader doesn't read it twice. A string equal to the trigger's
`aria-label` is caught without it.

side.description:
The trigger's side the bubble opens on: `bottom` (the default) or `top`
stack it, `left` or `right` set it beside the trigger, vertically centred
(the nav rail). It flips to the other side when it would leave the window.

sideOffset.description: The gap (px) between the trigger and the bubble.

Badge.description: A small tinted flag beside a title: a word or two, in capitals.

LiveBadge.description: A dark status pill with a pulsing dot: data on the card is updating live.

StatusDot.description: A small dot that marks a status beside its words; decorative, so the words carry it.

className.description: Its colour (`text-positive`) and place in a line. It's the text colour by default.

Spinner.description:
Shared loading indicator. Wraps the ldrs "waveform" loader so every loading
state across the app shares one look. Callers keep their own layout wrapper
(e.g. `.page-empty`, `.loading-screen`) for centring and spacing.

ButtonSpinner.description:
Compact busy indicator for buttons. Uses the ldrs "ring" loader so buttons
show a smooth rotating arc instead of a spinning icon. Colour is inherited
from the button via `currentColor`, so it works on both primary (white text)
and secondary/icon buttons.

LoadingState.description:
A page's first load: the spinner over a line saying what's coming, centred
in the content area. A status region, so the line is announced.

label.description: What's loading, as a sentence that ends in an ellipsis: "Loading usage…".

Banner.description:
A message above a page: icon, title, a line under it, then Dismiss and
Retry on the right. `error` is a failure. Dismiss hides this title until it changes or the banner
unmounts, so a poll that fails the same way again doesn't bring it back; a
caller renders it only while there's an error, which is what resets it.

description.description: One short line under the title: how old what's on screen is, or what happens next.

onRetry.description: Shows Retry, busy until the returned promise settles.

EmptyState.description:
The shared "nothing here yet" page: faded placeholder rows (with a lock badge
when the list is locked), a title, a short explanation and an optional action, centred
in the content region. Every view's blank state goes through this so they
line up on one rhythm and one measure.

actions.description: Controls below the description, usually a retry button.

description.description: A line or two naming what will fill the page, or why it can't.

isLocked.description:
A lock badge over the placeholder rows, for a list that can't fill until
the user acts (admin access needed) rather than one waiting for data.

EmptyStateDescription.description: A line of explanation under the title — also for extra notes the `actions` add.

role.description: `status` for a note that appears in answer to an action, so it's announced.

DataList.description:
A `<dl>` of DataRows: each row is a `<div>` holding a `<dt>` label and a
`<dd>` value, so the pairs read as a description list.

children.description: DataRows, as direct children (fragments are fine).

DataListStack.description:
DataLists grouped by topic, one after another: a hairline between groups,
with 12px of air either side of it.

DataRow.description: One label and value. Render it in a DataList, which sets its spacing.

Readout.description:
A large labelled number (live speed, data used), as a term and description:
render it inside a `<dl>`.

icon.description: A glyph before the label: the direction arrow.

spokenValue.description:
What a screen reader hears instead, when the visible number is animating
("182 Mbps" while the digits still count up to it).

ReadoutValue.description: A number and its unit, on their own, at a readout's size.

spokenValue.description:
What a screen reader hears instead, when the visible number is animating
("182 Mbps" while the digits still count up to it).

MetricValue.description:
A numeric readout that eases toward its latest value each poll (up or down),
matching the Traffic readouts. On first paint it shows the value outright
— the ease only kicks in when a subsequent poll changes the number.

BarMeter.description:
Four rising bars, some lit: signal strength or a rating at a glance. Visual
only; whatever it sits in says the value in words or with role="meter".

className.description: The bars' colour (`text-status-positive`), and their place in a row.

isDimmed.description: Grey bars that read as inactive: a stale rating waiting on a new test.

ListRow.description: A whole-row button in a card's list that opens something, with a trailing chevron.

children.description: The row's content: an icon tile, a title and its description.

isDisabled.description:
Inert for now (results that are being replaced): no hover, no action. It
keeps its look and its place in the Tab order.

trailing.description: Before the chevron, right-aligned: a meter, a value.

IconTile.description:
A rounded square holding an item's glyph, tinted by what the item is. It
takes a ref and extra props, so it can be a Tooltip's trigger.

className.description: The glyph's colour, which the tint follows, and the tile's place in its row.

IconTileButton.description: An IconTile that opens something: hover deepens the tint and lifts it a pixel.

className.description: The glyph's colour, which the tint follows, and the tile's place in its row.

isDisabled.description: Inert while what it opens is being replaced: no hover, no action, same look.

label.description: Names it: the glyph alone says nothing to a screen reader.

Card.description:
The panel surface, clipped to its rounded corners. Build it from a
CardHeader, a CardBody and an optional CardFooter, or lay out your own
content in it.

as.description:
`section` (the default) is named by its CardHeader's title, so give it one.
`div`, `li` or `ul` for a card with no header: a list's rows, a card in a
list, or a list that is one card.

isDivided.description: A hairline between each of its children: a list that is one card.

shouldClip.description: False for a card whose content pops out of it, such as a row's menu.

CardBody.description: The padded body. A little top padding gives the content more room below the title than above it.

CardFooter.description: A sunken band below the body, flush to the card's edges: a footnote or status.

CardHeader.description: The card's 44px title row: an icon, the title and its actions.

actions.description: Controls or a badge at the end of the row.

Collapsible.description: Shows and hides a panel from a trigger: a card's details, a group's rows.

as.description: `li` for a group in a list.

children.description: A CollapsibleTrigger and a CollapsiblePanel, wherever the layout puts them.

hasFocusFrame.description:
Rings the whole collapsible (trigger and open panel) when the trigger has
keyboard focus, instead of the trigger alone: for a trigger that spans a
card's or group's header.

CollapsiblePanel.description:
What the trigger shows and hides, growing and shrinking to its height; out
of the page, and the accessibility tree, while closed.

CollapsibleTrigger.description:
The button that opens and closes the panel; it says which (aria-expanded)
and what it controls. `data-panel-open` is set while open, for styling.

DotSeparator.description:
A dot gets 8px of air on each side: the rows it sits in space their items at
6px, and its margin adds 2px for the dot alone, so the gaps between other
items in the same row stay at 6px.

InlineMeta.description: Inline metadata chunks separated by a tertiary dot.

shouldTruncate.description: Keep the items on one line, each ellipsizing as space runs out.

TitleBar.description:
The full-width bar across the window's top, which drags the window. It
stays above the scrolling content, so nothing (buttons, tooltips, escaped
absolutes) can ever paint over it.

brand.description: The product mark and name, at the start.

controls.description: At the end: WindowButtons, on a frameless window.

TitleBarStatus.description: The connection status beside the brand: a dot (pulsing unless neutral) and its words, announced as they change.

WindowButton.description:
Minimise or close the window. Out of the Tab order, like a native title
bar's: otherwise the first Tab lands here instead of the nav rail, and a
stray Enter closes the window.

NavItem.description: One rail button: a page, or an action such as the theme switch.

isActive.description: The current page's item: tinted, with the accent bar.

label.description: Names the item, which shows only its glyph; also its tooltip.

NavRail.description:
The narrow icon-only rail down the window's left side. It stays above the
content column, like the title bar.

footer.description: Utilities at the bottom edge, below a hairline: settings, the theme switch.

label.description: Accessible name for the navigation landmark.

PageHeader.description:
The top of every page but Home: an icon chip (or a back button), the title
with a line under it, and actions at the end, over a full-width divider. It
sits above the page content (z-20), so its tooltips aren't painted over by
the content they drop into. The actions hold their size, so a long
description wraps instead of squeezing them.

actions.description: Controls at the end of the header (help, refresh, the page's main action).

description.description:
The line under the title. It fades in when it first shows, and again each
time `status` clears. `null` keeps the line's height while there's nothing
to show; leave it out to have no line.

icon.description: The page's nav glyph, in a chip: a top-level page.

onBack.description: A back button in the chip's place: a page layered over a tab.

status.description: Shown in the description's place while something loads or runs ("Checking…").

helpers.POLLING_DESCRIPTION: The second line for a page whose data polls: a failure there heals itself.
helpers.PortalProvider: Sets where the library's dialogs inside it portal to.
helpers.cn:
Join class names, skipping falsy ones, and let later Tailwind utilities win
over earlier ones that set the same thing: `cn('px-12', className)` with
`className="px-8"` gives `px-8`. Use it wherever a component merges its own
classes with a `className` from outside; plain joins can use `cx`.
helpers.useCountUp:
Eases a displayed number toward `target` each animation frame, so the value
visibly counts up or down instead of snapping. Used for the speed-test cells
and the live-traffic readouts.
helpers.useLatestRef:
A ref that always holds the latest `value`, for callbacks, timers and frame
loops that must read fresh props without re-subscribing.

The ref is written in a layout effect rather than during render, so a render
React throws away never leaks into it. Read it only outside render.
helpers.usePortalContainer: The element a PortalProvider above names for overlays, or null for in place.
helpers.usePresence:
Whether an element that animates out should still be mounted.

Rendering `{isActive && <X />}` drops the element the moment `isActive` turns
false, so a leave animation never gets to play. Render `<X />` while this
returns true instead, and style it as leaving while `isActive` is false: it
mounts as soon as `isActive` turns true and unmounts `exitMs` after it turns
false, which should match the length of the leave animation. Turning active
again before then cancels the unmount.
